decisions.question: D10-Q03
decisions.rule: Each of the five key kits is one USB stick with full-disk encryption (LUKS2, AES, a passphrase per kit) holding the kit's four private keys, plus a paper copy kept sealed with it. The paper copy is the kit's 32-byte secret, from which dytallix-root-sign derives the four keys (FIPS 205 key generation from SHAKE256-derived seeds), written as one checked line, so it can be copied by hand and recreates the kit.

decisions.question: D10-Q03
decisions.rule: The keys are made on a laptop booted from a Debian live USB with networking off, using the release's static dytallix-root-sign checked against the release SHA-256. Private keys go straight to the kit sticks and never touch the laptop's disk or a networked system; only public key records and proofs of possession leave the ceremony.

decisions.question: D10-Q03
decisions.rule: The five kits are kept in three or more places the founder controls or trusts, never three kits in one place, so no single fire or burglary reaches the three-kit threshold.

unset: The ceremony itself, its session and the kit sticks (founder actions)
